ideas.name: Goldman Roll Spread Pressure
ideas.claim: WTI calendar spreads narrowed during the commodity index roll window. The paper describes entering a short near-month and long deferred-month spread before the roll and unwinding it during the roll.
ideas.quote: The only difference is that Strategy 1 front-runs the Goldman roll by 10 business days, while Strategy 2 front-runs it by just 5 business days.
ideas.mechanism: Predictable index roll order flow pressures the spread between maturing and deferred futures.

rules.market: S&P GSCI energy futures, including WTI crude oil
rules.timeframe: Daily; positions held for 5 or 10 business days
rules.entry: Short the maturing contract and buy the deferred contract 5 or 10 business days before the corresponding roll date.
rules.exit: Unwind the spread on the corresponding index roll date.
rules.filters: Trade when the S&P GSCI rolls the commodity.

ideas.claimed_result: For 2000–2010, the paper reports 4.43% unlevered annual excess return for its energy portfolio under the 10-day strategy. For WTI, the reported difference between average roll yields in the first and last five days of the 15-day window was 0.47 percentage points.
required_data: S&P GSCI roll calendar and contract schedule
